claim: Two critical vulnerabilities
note: need the NSA post itself and the CVE IDs

claim: Found using frontier AI (ChatGPT) by Calif, then Wiz and OpenAI; 'a complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve'
The 'most severe' flaws ever detected by AI
Calif 'mistakenly published a video' showing basic details of how the flaws could be used
by: PHP Foundation (as reported by the BBC)
note: Calif's own account needed

claim: Criminals are using AI to 'vibe code' an attack method
Amazon and Cloudflare saw sites being probed for the flaw
note: second-hand; need AWS or Cloudflare statements

claim: No evidence yet that hackers have exploited the flaw
Attackers could take control of affected web servers without authentication and steal data
by: Paul Spain, Gorilla Cyber Security; Woodward

claim: Where immediate remediation is not feasible, take the system offline until fully mitigated
by: UK NCSC; NSA; EU and Australian counterparts

claim: Wikipedia (parts), Edinburgh council, French government sites, the University of Geneva, online shops and the BBC affected or taken offline
Two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each CVSS v4.0 9.2, fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35
The flaws are CVSS 10.0
by: social posts on 20 October, relayed by a vendor and a news site
note: contradicted by a primary source. The PHP Foundation: 'a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2)'. Daubois traces it to a social post relayed by Phoenix Security and to watchTowr via Cyber Daily.

claim: Unauthenticated RCE over HTTP against Apache mod_php with default settings, before any application code runs
Remote code execution is confirmed on PHP-FPM
by: PHP Foundation blog; GHSA-6wmf for the session path
note: GHSA-w8hw (CVE-2026-109618): 'no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI'. The Foundation blog: RCE 'was also confirmed on PHP-FPM through application-level code paths'. GHSA-6wmf (CVE-2026-109619): session lifecycle RCE 'validated against mod_php and FPM'. The accounts may refer to different CVEs.

claim: The fix removes longjmp() for out-of-memory errors in favour of a delayed soft OOM at the next VM safe point and a hard OOM via _exit(); the changelog line is 'Avoid state corruption via bailout'
The 8.5.12 fix may be incomplete, or there is a third, different bug
by: Fediverse posts relayed to oss-security by Aaron Rainbolt and Yves-Alexis Perez
note: Per a Matrix channel, Canonical asked PHP and 'was told that it's unrelated and not a real issue'. Second-hand. Nothing from PHP on the list at capture.

claim: All PHP versions from 5 onwards are affected by at least one of the flaws
note: The CVE records list only 8.2 to 8.5 with defaultStatus 'unaffected'. php.net published source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, which implies they are affected. A scanner that trusts the CVE record will miss 7.4 to 8.1.

claim: Updating is the only complete mitigation; the configuration measures reduce exposure to specific paths and do not make an installation safe
A web application firewall may provide some protection until systems are patched
note: Swiss BACS: 'Even a web application firewall alone is not sufficient.' Cloudflare says its rules blocked the traffic it saw and that attackers mutated payloads to get past them.

claim: Pre-authentication RCE was confirmed against WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, MediaWiki, Roundcube, Magento, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, Laravel, Symfony and WHMCS
by: Calif; Wiz for WordPress and Drupal
note: Two researcher parties, no third-party reproduction in the vault. The demo videos were not downloaded.

claim: Roughly 70% of the Internet is affected
by: Wiz (headline, X post); BBC attributing Wiz
note: The BBC was 'unable to independently verify that figure'. Wiz's body text says 70% of websites and cites no measurement.

claim: PHP is used by almost 70% of websites
by: Cloudflare; OpenAI ('an estimated 70%'); Wiz body text
note: None of the three cites the survey it comes from. A share of websites using PHP is an upper bound on exposure, not a count of vulnerable systems.

claim: Something like 30 million websites could be affected
note: No basis given.

claim: PHP is exposed on 2,608,039 internet-facing hosts
About 6,000 potentially affected resources in Latvia, a few hundred in the public sector
note: Primary source, one country, says 'potentially'.

claim: 674 products in the NCSC-NL inventory: 206 vulnerable, 46 fixed, 418 under investigation, 3 not vulnerable
by: NCSC-NL, counted by this site from the file at commit cca173c64ec5
note: Counted, not quoted. NCSC-NL calls unbacked entries 'investigation leads'.

claim: The flaws were found by researchers using frontier AI under OpenAI's Patch the Planet initiative
note: All three research parties say AI was used. Calif: 'No special harness, or access to models that weren't generally available to everyone were used'. Calif does not name a model; Wiz names Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-5.6 Sol and Wiz Atlas; OpenAI's blog reportedly names GPT-5.6 Sol but is blocked.

claim: Calif found the flaws first: discovery 1 August, hash commitment 5 August, report to PHP 11 August
note: The hash tweet is dated 5 August 2026 on X; its pre-image has not been published, so what it commits to cannot be checked.

claim: OpenAI independently reported the same root cause on 11 August, with further vectors on 18 September
note: The GitHub advisories credit amyb-oai among four reporters. OpenAI's own post credits Calif's discovery 'using GPT-5.6 Sol' and Wiz; an X Community Note disputes OpenAI's role.

claim: Wiz Research independently discovered the first flaw on 19 August and reported on 24 August
note: Wiz's X post says 'Wiz Research uncovers' with no credit to Calif or OpenAI; the blog thanks both.

claim: The GitHub advisories credit four reporters: lcfr-hax (Calif), sagitzadik-wiz (Wiz), amyb-oai (OpenAI) and tomash-areion
note: tomash-areion is not named in the PHP Foundation's thanks and appears nowhere else on this beat.

claim: The out-of-memory issue was found in a 2024 audit by Quarkslab (funded through OSTIF and the Sovereign Tech Agency) but exploitation was not proven, so it was not fixed
note: Two parties agree. The Foundation calls the delay 'a structural failure'. Cloudflare lists Quarkslab among the 2026 disclosers; nobody else does.

claim: Frontier AI found the flaw ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare
note: Amazon reports an exploit attempt against a honeypot on 17 October, four days before disclosure, from an actor whose source of exploit information is unknown.

claim: The most severe flaws ever detected by AI
note: Wiz's own wording is 'among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history'. OpenAI: 'one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory'.

claim: On 20 October at about 15:00 UTC the two CVE IDs began circulating on forums and social media with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score; no technical details leaked
note: Primary party. The Foundation does not say who or where.

claim: The leak started with an anonymous Hacker News post citing a reliable source, which came down after screenshots spread; a screenshot of the 'PHP2Shell tool' credited to Calif.io and a short exploitation video also went up and came down
by: Alexandre Daubois (PHP security team, personal blog)
note: Contradicts the Foundation's 'no technical details leaked' and The Hacker News's 'a proof-of-concept exploit leaked'. No copy of the post, screenshot or video is in the vault.

claim: watchTowr confirmed in public that the bugs were real and posted both CVE numbers before the release
by: Daubois; CERT-EU lists a watchTowr X post among public reports

claim: Calif mistakenly published a video around 20:00 UTC on 20 October showing its proof of concept against a number of targets; copies circulated and 'contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs'
note: Calif's own page does not mention a leak or a deleted video; it embeds two demo videos. Whether one of them is the deleted video is unknown.

claim: Mitigation advice given to a few critical-infrastructure providers from about 23:00 UTC on 20 October may have leaked
Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo on 21 October at 07:41 UTC by publishing built images containing the fix
note: Chainguard reportedly does not dispute the time but denies leaking (Techzine, blocked by a bot challenge; snippet only).

claim: The release moved forward from 22 October 14:00 UTC to 21 October 14:00 UTC because of the leak
by: PHP Foundation; php.net pre-announcement; Wiz thread ('Apply the Oct 22 security release')
note: The php.net ChangeLog still dates all four releases 22 October. Wiz's X thread still says 22 October.

claim: The flaws were disclosed on 22 October 2026
note: contradicted by a primary source. Primary sources put the release at 21 October: GHSAs 13:34Z, tags 13:35Z, CVE records 13:48Z and 13:54Z, GitHub release 14:06Z.

claim: The fixes were released at 14:00 UTC on 21 October
note: CERT-EU says 13:30 UTC; the tags and advisories are stamped 13:34 to 13:35 UTC; the GitHub release 14:06 UTC; the php.net feed entries carry 00:05 to 00:35 UTC, which are authoring times, not publication times.

claim: The pre-announcement was published at 19:30 UTC on 20 October
note: The php.net feed says 20:32 UTC; oss-security relayed it at 20:22:51 UTC, so it was public by then.

claim: There is no evidence yet that hackers have exploited the flaw
by: Ryan Austin, Calif, on Radio 4, 08:00 BST 22 October

claim: CISA has not observed exploitation; neither CVE is in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
note: Catalog version 2026.10.21 fetched 2026-10-22T08:15Z, 1,754 entries. A point-in-time negative finding.

claim: Reports of active exploitation exist
note: The only agency saying so, and it does not say whose reports.

claim: An exploit attempt hit an Amazon honeypot on 17 October from an anonymisation network, and proof-of-concept attempts started about 02:00 UTC on 21 October
by: CJ Moses, Amazon, via The Hacker News
note: Amazon's own post has not been found.

claim: Cloudflare observed attack traffic targeting its customers after the leak, with attackers mutating payloads
note: Primary party, no volumes.

claim: Amazon and Cloudflare saw sites being probed for the flaw
note: Second-hand, but consistent with what both companies have said themselves.

claim: Automated exploitation attempts were seen in Latvia; none succeeded
note: Primary source.

claim: Criminals are using AI to 'vibe code' an attack method
If an immediate update is not feasible, take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated
note: X post 13:45:58Z 21 October (10.1 million views at capture) and the press release.

claim: Organisations that cannot update immediately, or that run PHP 8.1 or older, should take PHP-based systems offline
'Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated'
by: UK NCSC, as quoted by the BBC
note: That sentence is not on the NCSC page as captured at 08:09Z on 22 October. The page's offline advice is step 4 of 6 and is worded differently. The page was modified at 07:30Z that morning. The sentence's opening matches the Canadian CCCS text.

claim: The UK's NCSC, the NSA and their counterparts in the EU and Australia advise taking systems offline where patching is not feasible
note: contradicted by a primary source. Australia's ACSC gives no offline advice. CERT-EU says isolate. The Netherlands, Italy, Japan and New Zealand give no offline advice.

claim: Parts of Wikipedia, Edinburgh council, French government sites, the University of Geneva, online shops and the BBC were affected or taken offline
note: Not captured from any of the named organisations.

claim: Latvia restricted access from abroad to several state digital resources, possibly until 26 October; lsm.lv and 112.lv were restored by 20:00 UTC
note: The one documented case of government services being pulled from the public internet, from the agency itself.

claim: The risks require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies
note: No CISA emergency directive was visible on the CISA home page at capture.

claim: ČVUT (Czech Technical University in Prague) is dealing with a cyber attack on its IT infrastructure that it calls part of worldwide attempts to hit PHP websites; the active attack was stopped and some systems were taken offline as a precaution
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-cvut (open), statement 1. The organisation's own words describe attempts and a stopped attack, not a successful compromise. The queue's Facebook capture of ČVUT's post was not promoted: it holds no statement text (login wall).

claim: It is not yet clear whether the unavailability of ČVUT's sites really relates to PHP2Shell; the community has found no evidence of real exploitation
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-cvut (open), statement 2.

claim: Unauthorised programs were found on 20 October on some servers of GMO's FX automated-trading VPS (お名前.com デスクトップクラウド); 26,739 servers may be affected, trading-account logins may have been taken, and fraudulent operations on trading accounts have been reported
by: GMO Internet Group, via J-CAST / Yahoo! News Japan
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-gmo-fx-vps (open), statement 1. The compromise is stated by GMO; what is disputed is any link to php2shell.

claim: The GMO article does not name PHP or php2shell as the cause; the link exists only in other outlets' juxtaposition
by: the source watch (reading of the same capture)
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-gmo-fx-vps (open), statement 2. The curator's reading of the capture agrees: PHP appears only in related-article links.

claim: DMM halted services from 22:00 on 21 October for emergency maintenance to respond to a vulnerability found in external software it uses; no personal data leaked
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-dmm (open), statement 1.

claim: DMM told Sankei it cannot say more than its announcement and would not confirm a link to PHP
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-dmm (open), statement 2.

claim: Valtec halted services and may have leaked personal data after a cyberattack targeting the PHP vulnerability
by: Valtec (first statement, 22 October), via INTERNET Watch
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-valtec (resolved). The company retracted its PHP attribution the same day: the cause was a vulnerability in its own service.

claim: Valtec's correction: the attack exploited a vulnerability in its own service, not PHP; it confused the two because it was handling the PHP vulnerability at the time
by: Valtec (correction), via INTERNET Watch (same article, updated)
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record compromise-valtec (resolved), statement 2: the resolution.

claim: The BSI has found no cases of exploitation so far, and the absence of reports suggests many operators have patched
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record exploitation-germany-netherlands (open), statement 1.

claim: Abuse of the PHP2Shell flaw has been reported: several security firms report attack attempts; whether any succeeded is unclear, and Previdian says attackers did not manage to execute PHP or upload files
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record exploitation-germany-netherlands (open), statement 2. The headline says abuse; the body says attempts.

claim: 50 sites went dark over php2shell, 2 of them still dark at 18:36 UTC on 22 October
note: From the source watch's contradiction ledger, record sites-taken-offline (open), statement 2. The other statement there (10 operators, the site's own impact ledger) has no evidence source to cite, so it is not recorded here. Each tracker row is only as good as the source it cites.

claim: 724 products in the NCSC-NL inventory at 18:36 UTC on 22 October, now in 27 per-letter files: for each CVE 216 vulnerable, 61 fixed, 440 under investigation, 6 not vulnerable
note: Counted by the curator from the captured files. Supersedes by time the 674-product count at commit cca173c64ec5 (08:40 UTC), claim scale-ncsc-nl in claude-story-site's file; that count was right for its time.

claim: QNAP PSIRT observed scanning activity and exploitation attempts against the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in the wild, and blocked attempted attacks on QNAP's website, online store and cloud services
note: A vendor's first-hand observation of attempts, not of a successful compromise. Its advisory says QNAP has no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products (qnap-qsa-26-18).

claim: QNAP products are affected (QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud, QuMagie, Note Station 3, QNE, QVR Surveillance on ARM32, TVR OS); fixed versions pending, users told to keep devices off the internet

PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 are affected through the management web interface; fixes pending; Palo Alto is not aware of malicious exploitation against its products and rates it HIGH (CVSS-B 8.7) in its product
note: Palo Alto's product vectors score availability impact only (VC:N/VI:N/VA:H), not code execution, unlike the 9.2 PHP vendor score it also shows (claim two-cves-9.2).

claim: Cisco is investigating seven products; no Cisco product is yet known to be affected, and Cisco PSIRT is not aware of malicious use
Fortinet is investigating FortiDDoS, FortiDDoS-F, FortiClient Cloud Services, FortiSOAR and FortiSOAR PaaS; FortiOS and others are confirmed not impacted
NÚKIB: updating is the only solution; fixed in PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; information enabling exploitation is publicly available
note: Agrees with the fixed versions in claim two-cves-9.2.

claim: The Swiss Federal Office for Cyber Security (BACS) knows of no attacks in Switzerland
note: English from the source watch reader's translation.

claim: Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara said no damage had been reported
by: Japanese government, via Kyodo (Chinese edition) and Koran Jakarta
note: Sits alongside the GMO FX VPS compromise and Valtec's (retracted) PHP attribution, both in Japan on the same days; neither is attributed to php2shell by the company.

claim: Mostly automated exploitation attempts against private and state systems in Latvia have so far failed; about 6,000 resources in Latvia could be affected, several hundred in the public sector
by: CERT.LV deputy head, via Delfi (LTV Panorāma)
note: Adds a source and the 6,000 estimate to claim latvia-attempts (claude-story-site). English from the source watch reader's translation.

claim: About 22 million servers are exposed (an estimate attributed to Palo Alto Networks)
note: Second-hand; Palo Alto's own advisory (paloalto-psirt-cve-2026-109618) gives no such figure. Not comparable with claim scale-2.6m-hosts (Censys hosts) or scale-30m (websites).

claim: 1.5 million of 2.6 million hosts ran unpatched PHP (Censys data)
note: The 2.6 million agrees with claim scale-2.6m-hosts. English from the source watch reader's translation.

claim: About 5.1 million IPs run PHP (VirusTotal analysis), 1.1 million disclose their version, about 272,000 run supported branches and about 758,000 run end-of-life versions
note: A different measure (IPs) from Censys's 2.6 million hosts. English from the source watch reader's translation.

claim: To the PHP Foundation's knowledge there has been no successful attempt at remote code execution
by: Elizabeth Barron, PHP Foundation executive director, to WIRED and The Verge
note: Break-in question. Stated on 21-22 October; 'to our knowledge'.

claim: Observed activity since disclosure remains limited to scanning, fingerprinting and non-working exploits, with no known compromises
note: Break-in question.

claim: No breach at a real organisation had been confirmed by the time the fixes were released; watchTowr's decoy servers recorded attempts
note: Break-in question. The same page's 22 October update says vendors now report exploitation beyond honeypots, not yet confirmed by agencies.

claim: Patchstack received reports of multiple active exploitation incidents from hosting partners by 07:34 UTC on 21 October, and says it has confirmed multiple active exploitation incidents
by: Patchstack, via Recorded Future and Insurance Business
note: Break-in question. The strongest vendor claim of real incidents, but second-hand here, and no victim organisation is named. Recorded Future: public evidence 'remains insufficient to establish the extent of successful compromise'.

claim: PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild; it is unclear whether any of the observed attempts would have succeeded on real-world systems
by: Amazon (CJ Moses, AWS CISO), via WIRED, BleepingComputer, The Register and SecurityWeek
note: Both halves are Amazon's own words: 'exploited' here means attempts seen on honeypots and sensors, not confirmed break-ins.

claim: PHP2Shell is being exploited in the wild at scale, mostly through PHP's session upload-progress mechanism
by: Hadrian, via The Register, TechTarget and Insurance Business

claim: Huntress had not observed exploitation across its partner systems
Cloudflare observed exploit attempts in spikes of thousands, rising to millions by the evening of 21 October; these describe attack attempts and do not by themselves establish successful compromises
by: Cloudflare (Daniele Molteni to USA Today; Matthew Prince via The Verge; counts via Fortune)

claim: At least one Chinese IP address unsuccessfully attempted to exploit PHP2Shell to deploy a webshell
A startup owner says hackers stole their source code, exposed cookie data and leaked legal documents through the PHP bug
by: an unnamed startup owner, via Fortune (linking to a post on X)
note: Break-in question. The only claimed break-in in this batch. 'Allegedly' in Fortune's words; no company is named and nothing shown links the theft to php2shell. The person is not named here. Not a named organisation, so it does not contradict the statement on /compromise/.

claim: The PHP vulnerabilities were exploited days before they were patched
note: The headlines say exploited; both bodies describe an attempt on an Amazon honeypot on 17 October and quote the PHP Foundation that no successful RCE is known.

claim: Chainguard independently found the vulnerability on 16 October with an AI harness, and published fixed builds early because vendors in the disclosure channel reported active exploitation overnight on 20-21 October
by: Dan Lorenc, Chainguard CEO, to TechTarget
note: Chainguard's side of claim chainguard (claude-story-site, disputed). Lorenc does not dispute publishing early; he disputes the PHP Foundation's account that Chainguard had the patch early for its customers.
